in_text_mentions: A non‐contrast brain CT confirmed the prenatal findings, revealing cystic dilation of the posterior fossa, absence of the cerebellar vermis, and enlargement of the fourth ventricle. The straight sinus and torcula were positioned superior to the lambdoid suture, all consistent with DWM (Figure 1). Additionally, the CT scan demonstrated moderate dilation of the right lateral ventricle without signs of transependymal CSF permeation. No evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, midline shift, or other significant abnormalities was noted, and white‐gray matter differentiation appeared normal (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: he MRI revealed a well-defined extra axial cystic lesion in the posterior fossa in the midline communicating with the fourth ventricle.
